part1: Part 1 · Lesson: learn the words first
goal_h: What you will be able to do
goal: After about 4 minutes you can explain 7 terms that appear in the news below, in your own words. Everything in Part 1 is background teaching (my own explanation), not newsletter facts; it follows the wiki glossary and concept pages.

terms.one: A package is the protective case and wiring that connect a tiny silicon chip (a die) to a circuit board. An OSAT is a company that assembles and tests chips for others.
terms.pic: The die is a tiny engine; the package is the engine block with all the pipes and plugs.
terms.why: A design only works if it can be packaged: heat, power and signals all have to get in and out.

terms.one: A chiplet is a small die that works together with other dies inside one package, instead of making one giant chip.
terms.pic: Building a house from prefabricated rooms instead of casting it as one block of concrete.
terms.why: Small dies are cheaper to make well and can mix technologies, but the links between dies become part of your design.

terms.one: Pitch is the distance between neighbouring connections; smaller pitch means more connections in the same area. Flip-chip joins dies with tiny solder balls, while hybrid bonding presses copper pads directly together, so the pitch can be much smaller.
terms.pic: Solder balls are a few big plugs; hybrid bonding is a dense field of tiny pins.
terms.why: Denser links give more bandwidth for less energy between stacked dies, so designers must plan them early.

terms.one: HBM is a tower of stacked memory dies placed right next to the processor. The base die at the bottom of the tower manages the connection to the processor.
terms.pic: A tall car park next to a shop: many cars (data) can move at once.
terms.why: AI chips depend on HBM bandwidth, and a customised base die makes memory part of the chip design.

terms.one: The memory wall means a processor can compute faster than memory can deliver data, so moving data, not calculating, becomes the limit.
terms.pic: A chef who cooks in seconds but waits an hour for the ingredients.
terms.why: Moving data costs more energy than computing on it, so architects try to move less data, for example with near-memory computing.

terms.one: EDA is the software used to design chips. RTL is code that describes what the hardware does; verification checks it works before manufacturing; 'shift left' means finding bugs earlier.
terms.pic: RTL is the blueprint written as code; verification is the building inspector who checks the blueprint before anything is built.
terms.why: A bug found after manufacturing is far more expensive, which is why AI agents are being tried on verification and exploration first.

terms.one: A foundry manufactures chips that other companies design. A node name such as 18A or 2 nm marks a manufacturing generation; the number is a marketing label, not a literal size.
terms.pic: The foundry is a print shop and the node is its printing technology; you bring the artwork, your design.
terms.why: Your design must follow the foundry's rules for its node, and capacity at advanced nodes is limited.

quiz.q: What does hybrid bonding do differently from flip-chip?
quiz.why: Hybrid bonding presses copper pads together without solder, so connections can be much closer.
